The FOMC statement points to solid real-side momentum and ongoing disinflation with policy held at a restrictive 5.25–5.50% and QT continuing until there is greater confidence inflation is moving sustainably to 2%. Incorporating the latest SLOOS, however, tilts the balance more cautious: banks, on net, report tighter lending standards and weaker demand for C&I loans, broad tightening in CRE (including by foreign banks), and tighter consumer credit with rising delinquencies/charge-offs. Banks cite the economic outlook and risk as key reasons for tightening and expect standards to remain tight. These credit-supply headwinds imply a drag on business capex and CRE, reinforcing disinflation but posing downside risks to growth and amplifying sensitivity to financial stress. Net effect: the macro read remains constructive but is tempered by restrictive bank credit, supporting the Fed’s “higher for longer until confident” stance and vigilance to emerging strains.
